Multiplayer is out of scope by name under the shared contract's rule 1, so this is a genuine waiver and not a dormant gap: the divergence's SHAPE, not merely today's content, is multiplayer. The sim now expresses this directly on `is_allowed` (not a separate `is_allowed_at_neow` flag as before), matching C#'s member; see guard N2. The executed unreachability proof is guard N1's.

Every card it can offer is multiplayer-only, so the effect is out of scope twice over -- the relic cannot be obtained (guard N1) and its payload does not exist in Ironclad single-player scope. Waived under the contract's multiplayer exclusion. The CardChoiceHistoryEntry bookkeeping (line 41) is replay history.

guards.issue: Recorded, DORMANT, as the one thing a reader should not conclude from the waivers above: the port is a stub, not a guarded no-op. If any future content ever puts Massive Scroll in a single-player run -- a hand-written test fixture, a conformance resync granting it by id, or the roster's own pool changing -- the relic does nothing at all instead of failing loudly, and the 3-card choice C# would offer is simply lost. The concrete unported thing that makes it live is multiplayer itself, which is permanently out of scope; filed as a dormant gap rather than folded into the AfterObtained waiver so the stub-ness stays visible to sweep C's stub census, which lists this relic under the "out-of-combat pickup effect, stub" family.
